label: information (terse / stub)
captures: terse standalone information/stub, few commas or colons; e.g. 'Originally Published 1822', 'Actress in dancing costume'

label: reference or list fragment
captures: reference/accession numbers, run-lengths, prices, list fragments; e.g. 'SRO No. series 119/144-148', '14 [1885], six nights', '6d. or 2s.'
example: SHOTLIST: 00:00:10 00:04:10 29/06/1989 OPENING OF PARLIAMENT - INT GVS HOUSE OF

label: part(s) of given name(s)
captures: terse name-part fragments, plus some reader-directions; e.g. 'Fitzgerald.', 'Miss Wallis..', 'In two columns.'

label: genre
captures: semicolon-separated genre/form tags; e.g. 'non-fiction; television arts'

label: information (terse / stub), comma-separated
captures: comma-separated terse information: imprints, credits, responsibility; e.g. 'Producer, STV', 'Printed by Stafford & Co., Netherfield'
example: Dismal = Daniel Finch, Earl of Nottingham.

label: sequential / timecoded description
captures: shotlist body: sequential and/or timecoded description; e.g. 'Pulls out through dock gates (2.30)'
example: SHOTLIST: gvs of woman at the Workers Education Association (WEA) answering an e

label: numeric value (date or reference)
captures: a bare number: a date or a reference/accession number; e.g. '27th June 1913.', '119/122'

label: information (descriptive / prose)
captures: longer, prose-like information/description; e.g. 'The drawing is undated and unsigned.', poster/photograph descriptions
greedy: Partly (broadest; longest of the information family)
example: The text mentions the census taking place on Sunday April 3rd - 1881 is the only

label: information (terse / stub) after colon
captures: field-label 'X: Y' statement; e.g. 'Tune: Boyne water.', 'Date of event depicted: 1879', 'Caption: ...'

label: other / unreliable
captures: isolated incoherent cluster (was CAT_06); predominantly moving-image bare 'non-fiction'; kept isolated, not interpreted
